DATE
Thursday, February 12, 2026 at 9 a.m. ET
CALL PARTICIPANTS
President and Chief Executive Officer — Robert W. Eifler
Chief Financial Officer — Richard B. Barker
Senior Vice President, Marketing and Contracts — Blake Denton
Senior Vice President, Operations — Angeli Kolaja
Vice President, Investor Relations — Ian MacPherson

TAKEAWAYS
Adjusted EBITDA
-- $232 million for the quarter and slightly above $1.1 billion for the full year, marginally surpassing prior guidance midpoint.
Free Cash Flow
-- $35 million in the quarter and $454 million for the year, as directly reported.
Revenue
-- $705 million for the quarter and $3.3 billion for the full year from contract drilling services.
Dividend
-- $0.50 per share declared for the current quarter, with $80 million returned to shareholders in Q4 via the quarterly dividend program.
Total Backlog
-- $7.5 billion as of February 11, 2026, up 30% year over year, and now exceeding current year backlog for 2027.
Major Contract Awards
-- Three-year, $473 million contract for Noble Great White in Norway; two-year, $292 million contract for Noble Johnny D’Souza in Nigeria with three 1-year options; multiple other notable awards in Trinidad, South America, U.S. Gulf, and Asia Pacific.
Backlog Conversion
-- Approximate $2.3 billion scheduled for revenue recognition in 2026, with a slightly greater amount already booked for 2027, marking "the first instance in many years" where year-two backlog exceeds year-one.
Capital Expenditures
-- $152 million in Q4, $497 million for the full year (net of insurance), and 2026 guidance of $590 million-$640 million, including project upgrades and reactivations.
Great White Project CapEx
-- Approximately $160 million expected spend, split equally between 2026 and 2027, to reactivate and certify the rig for Norway, targeting approximately $240 million EBITDA across the three-year contract.
Fleet Strategy
-- Sale of five jackups to Borr Drilling for $360 million completed; sale of Noble Resolve for $64 million expected to close in Q3; continued focus on high-end deepwater and CJ70 jackup markets.
Utilization Metrics
-- Contracted UDW fleet at 95% utilization including future starts, 82% when considering only currently working rigs, signaling a backlog build without full prompt fleet deployment.
Market Dayrates
-- Tier-one drillships securing around $400,000 per day, with lower-spec units ranging from low to high $300,000s per day in current fixtures.
Guidance for 2026
-- Total revenue of $2.8 billion-$3.0 billion (including $150 million reimbursable/other revenues), adjusted EBITDA range of $940 million-$1.02 billion, and anticipated flat Q1 adjusted EBITDA relative to Q4.
Future EBITDA Run Rate
-- Management outlined visibility to $1.3 billion of EBITDA and approximately $600 million in free cash flow in 2027 assuming current contracts and market rates.
Tax and Cash Flow Details
-- Expected 2026 cash taxes of 11%-12% of adjusted EBITDA and a favorable working capital reduction of roughly $100 million, partly from CapEx reimbursements.
SUMMARY
Management highlighted a robust $7.5 billion backlog, positioning
Noble Corporation

(
NE

+0.47%

for greater revenue recognition in 2027 than 2026 for the first time in many years. CEO Robert W. Eifler stated that "over 90% of our 24 floaters now contracted" gives direct line of sight to significant EBITDA and free cash flow uplift, with only minor additional contracting required to hit 2027 targets. CFO Richard B. Barker noted that the low end of next year's EBITDA guidance is fully covered by existing backlog and high-confidence options, excluding any need for dayrate improvement. Recent strategic fleet moves—most notably the sale of five jackups and the redeployment of the Noble Great White—support a capital-light, high-NAV fleet strategy focused on deepwater and harsh environment assets. Management characterized current deepwater rig contracting as resilient despite "Brent prices hovering around five-year lows" and described an increasing structural differentiation between prompt and future utilization rates. Dayrates remain near $400,000 for tier-one assets, with management expressing that increased activity and backlog depth, not crude price recoveries alone, are driving contract momentum.
Management provided that "the number of pieces that need to fall in place for a tight 2027 are substantially lower than what we have seen in quite some time," suggesting lower execution risk for upcoming cycles.
The company reported that "33% increase versus last year in open tenders and pretenders for floaters" now equates to approximately 100 rig years of open demand, excluding direct negotiations.
"This is a highly strategic investment with a compelling return profile, as we anticipate total EBITDA potential of approximately $240,000,000 over the three-year contract period." per management, with expected EBITDA recovery of project capital in two years and positioning the asset for long-term competitiveness in Norway.
Favorable working capital trends and recent asset sales, including $210 million in cash proceeds from the sale of five jackups in Q1 and an approximately $21 million cash deposit from the Noble Resolve sale in Q4, along with a $150 million seller note, enhance liquidity and balance sheet flexibility as per CFO Richard B. Barker.
The upcoming year features "weighting of adjusted EBITDA in the second half" due to fleet deployments and backlog conversion, but management does not anticipate a dramatic shift between first and second halves per current contracts.
INDUSTRY GLOSSARY
UDW
: Ultra-Deepwater; refers to offshore drilling operations at water depths greater than 7,500 feet.
CJ70 Jackup
: High-specification jackup drilling rig designed for harsh environment operations, particularly in Northwest Europe.
MPD
: Managed Pressure Drilling; an advanced drilling technique enabling more precise pressure control to improve operational efficiency and safety.
CM/L system
: Choke Manifold/Liquid system integrated for well control and pressure management on drillships.
BOP
: Blowout Preventer; a safety-critical device used to manage wellbore pressure and prevent uncontrolled hydrocarbon releases.
NAV
: Net Asset Value; the total value of assets minus liabilities, relevant to fleet valuation.
FIDs
: Final Investment Decisions; key project commitment milestones in the oil and gas industry.
D-class semis
: Sixth-generation semi-submersible rigs with dual (moored and DP) positioning capabilities and advanced design for deepwater operations.

We, as I repeat myself, but we are a better company today than we were before because of the scale we have built. And there are going to be opportunities out there.
We will continue to look at everything, and we will continue to be as picky as we ever have been on ensuring that any opportunity we look at sits in the right place for us as a company in terms of the type of asset and the quality of the asset. Great. Thanks a lot. Thank you.

I do not mean to suggest that this is a window in time, but I think the fact that they have kind of contracted prior to the seventh gens is the phenomenon of being at the right place in the right time for the right projects.
It is not a value decision by our customers, as you mentioned, which is a good thought, but I do not believe that is what is driving it at all. Got it. And then we have kind of long sought it. You know, the sixth gens, we need to see better utilization just to get another round of upward momentum in rates across the collective seventh- and sixth-gen marketplace. However, you know, the incremental rigs that probably the tightness in supply and demand, you know, crude price does matter for near-term projects.
And that is why we kind of outlined in our script the problem, not the answer. I personally am quite optimistic for 2027 for the reasons I mentioned in prepared remarks. But we need another, say, five rig contracts that we do not see anywhere out there today to come through to really get to an extremely tight market, call it. I am pretty confident that everything is set up to supply that. I do not think there is any reason that could not happen by 2027. Let me put it that way. But we are a little cautious to say we kind of have to see how 2026 plays out here right now.
I will say I think there are a lot of contracts that are going to get announced here, not just now. Well, just across the board over the next few months. And I think that obviously should all be well received. We are including all of that in our analysis, and we are pretty hopeful that here going into 2027, we have the various pieces for a tightening market. I appreciate the color. Thank you.
